title: How often should you get a massage?
excerpt: Once a month, once a week or only when it hurts? Sarah's honest answer, and why it depends on what you do all day.
content:
It's the question we hear most at the desk. The honest answer is that it depends on what your body does all week.

Desk all day

Once a month keeps shoulders and necks from locking up. More often if you're in pain.

Running or climbing

Every two or three weeks in training, and a few days after a big event, not the day before.

Just to switch off

Whenever you need it. There's no wrong answer to that one.

title: Massage in pregnancy: what to expect
excerpt: When it's safe to start, how you'll lie and what helps most in each trimester. Answers from Holly, who was a midwife for ten years.
content:
Pregnancy massage is one of our most booked treatments. Here's what it's like.

When can I start?

From 14 weeks. Before that, rest is the best treatment.

How will I lie?

On your side, with cushions under your bump and between your knees. Never on your front.

What helps most?

Lower back and hips in the second trimester, legs and feet in the third.

title: Five ways to a slower evening
excerpt: Small things we suggest after a treatment that work just as well on an ordinary Tuesday.
content:
What you do after a massage matters almost as much as the massage. These help any evening.

Warm water, then bed

A bath or a long shower an hour before sleep tells your body it's time.

Phone in another room

The single biggest thing. Use an old-fashioned alarm clock.

Something warm to drink

Mint or chamomile tea, nothing with caffeine after four.

title: Three stretches for desk workers
excerpt: Two minutes, three times a day, and your next massage will be less work for both of us.
content:
Most of the shoulders we see are desk shoulders. These three stretches help between visits.

Doorway chest stretch

Arms on the door frame, lean through gently for thirty seconds.

Chin tucks

Draw your chin back, as if making a double chin, ten times.

Seated twist

Turn from the waist, hand on the chair back, and hold for five breaths each side.
